reviews.text:
Harvey, my best friend of 15 years, was met with compassion, generosity, and emotional support through the last week and a half of his life. My baby was a medical mystery, but the team did everything in their power to figure out the etiology of his suffering (including recruiting opinions of multiple specialties) and ensure his comfortability through many days of poking and prodding.

Prices were reasonable, but most importantly I felt a kindness and empathy that is unmatched.

I cannot thank enough Dr. Tansey and Dr. Schumacher, as well as the oncology team, especially Michelle and Marcus. Thank you for easing our pain through this difficult time.

We recently had to make the awful decision to part with our sweet Tilly cat. Dr. Krebs and the MASH team were just incredible. It’s hard to deliver the kind of information we had to hear, but they were with us every step of the way with care, clarity of the issues, and possible outcomes. I have never felt in better hands. They really took the situation with the utmost care and sincerity and helped us make such an impossible call. You could tell the entire team honestly cared so much about Tilly, her quality of life, and giving her a peaceful departure surrounded by love. I couldn’t recommend this loving team more.

Can't say enough great things about this place.
My husband and I came in because we had to say the hardest goodbye to our bestfriend. When someone has to make that decision you are not in the best state of mind, and that's why I am greatful to MASH  West Hollywood. I felt that they were very compassionate and caring, from the person I first called on the phone to ask for some information to the nurses and doctors that attended us at the hospital. Every one of their staff exuded compassion, care, respect, understanding, and patience. Made our hardest day just a little bit better, knowing there are people that care for animals the way the staff here does.

The facility was also great, we were given our own room, it was nice and clean. We were able to sit with our pupper one last time and given all the time we wanted and needed. The pricing was also reasonable.

My baby's name was Sparky, a 16year old chihuahua mix. The bestest boy in the world ❤️ Our hearts are broken but I am glad we were able to give him a dignified ferwell and it was all possible because of this Hospital and I will always be greatful. Thank you again!!

Waited on hold for 30 minutes (after being transferred to Oncology) only to be told that the oncology team was unavailable and that I would need to call back the next day. When I asked if I could receive a convenient call back in hopes to schedule a consultation, I was told that they could take my information but could not guarantee a call back. It's strange to call and disclose the emotional shock of your your cat needing cancer treatment and then receive little consideration for the client experience, the time spent over the and the emotional energy it takes to navigate something like this. I did receive clarification through this interaction that this place is not in alignment with where I would like to take my cat for treatment. After hanging up, I called another specialty care center and scheduled an appointment within minutes. Some extra consideration for patients while navigating a sensitive and overwhelming process would prove beneficial for the MASH team and would help build trust between new clients and their operations.

I would strongly caution pet owners against bringing their pets here. My experience left me feeling that this hospital takes advantage of people at their most vulnerable.

I was out of town when my mom, who was pet sitting, brought my cat in with a urinary blockage. We were explicitly told that without immediate intervention, **he would die**. Either his bladder would rupture or he could go into cardiac arrest from toxins building up in his bloodstream.

Despite telling us this was a life-or-death emergency, they **refused to begin treatment until 80% of their highest estimate was paid upfront.** I was out of town frantically trying to arrange financing through CareCredit, and their staff failed to give me the correct payment instructions. I initially tried using my CareCredit card number like a normal credit card, only to eventually learn they required a different process—further delaying the emergency treatment they had just told me my cat needed to survive.

The final bill was **$7,695.06 for a Nov. 12–15 hospitalization.** Basically, a catheter, an IV and some urine/blood testing. Worse, my cat should have been discharged the night before, but I was told they were too busy to evaluate him for release. They kept him overnight as a result and then charged me for **another overnight AND morning hospitalization shift**, despite my picking him up that morning.

When I later questioned the bill and requested his medical records, I couldn't even get the complete records. They were finally provided only after I escalated the matter and began disputing the charges with my credit card company.

I understand emergency veterinary medicine is expensive, and I am grateful my cat survived. My complaint is not that lifesaving care costs money. It's that when someone tells you your pet will die without immediate treatment, you have essentially no bargaining power and based on my experience, this hospital's financial and billing practices exploit that vulnerability.

I would never bring my cat here again.

This place is predatory. Please do not go here. I called them when my dog wasn’t eating and they said to bring him in that night and they could see him. I waited four hours with no communication, and they finally said they didn’t have time to see him but could watch him overnight for $5,000. I made a half dozen trips here and the urgency to see or help my dog was so much lower than the urgency to collect payments. They charged $30 more per bottle of medicine than my local vet. They charged $9,000 more for a surgery I ended up getting successfully elsewhere.

I believe many of the people working here do care about animals, such as Dr. Norris, but the pricing model and policies are so predatory it’s infuriating. They will constantly tell you that it costs the same elsewhere, banking on the idea that you’re too emotionally spent to shop around, but you will find great care and more affordable prices almost anywhere else.

I'm going to be as objective as possible in the hope that this helps someone else in a situation like mine.

I brought my dog here because I needed an emergency ultrasound after a routine x-ray found a large mass on his spleen earlier that morning. They were kind enough to fit us in for a last-minute ultrasound (for a $255 emergency appointment fee).

The ultrasound confirmed that the mass had already ruptured.

I asked if they could operate in that moment. I was told it would cost at least another $4,000 more to do it that night and would not even want to tell me the full price of the surgery until I had the appointment with the surgeon.

Instead, they scheduled a pre-operative consultation for the following day (another $230), and surgery would have taken place the day after that even tho they knew my dog was already bleeding internally. (They sold me without telling me 1 pack of anti-hemorrhage Yunnan Baiyao herb supplements for $67.)

Right after he was discharged, he started urinating dark brown outside of the hospital. I immediately came back to let them know. Their response was essentially, "We'll stick to the game plan. We'll see you tomorrow for the first consultation.

Fortunately, my first vet choice, called me back early Monday morning and after I explained the situation. Their response was: "We need to operate immediately."

They came to my house to pick up my dog at no charge, performed another ultrasound at no charge, and took him straight into surgery without asking for a single dollar upfront.

The surgery was successful. Afterward, the surgeon told me that if we had waited one more day, my dog likely would not have survived.

I'm not writing this to hurt this establishment. The staff was very friendly, as you would expect when you're paying $1,000 for an emergency visit and ultrasound.

I'm writing this to help anyone who may find themselves in the same situation. If your pet has a life-threatening emergency — do not come here, trust your gut and act fast.

For me, choosing Sevilla Veterinary Hospital in Santa Monica saved my dog's life.

Not enough good things I can say about these folks. Been here twice, both due to needing urgent care after it looked like my dog injested sugar free gum. They were great ranging from engaging poison control, doing great triage and coming up with an appropriate treatment plan that took both my dogs welfare and my wallet into account and are so good at helping human clients with what are generally very stressful experiences. Both times, everyone from the front desk staff and techs, intake nurses, doctors, all capable, friendly and professional. Thank you so much for the superior care.

I just want to thank this hospital for taking care of my fur baby in her last moments. Outstanding services and the cremation package is pretty affordable and all the items are beautiful I’m so glad we found them and that my baby was here in her last moments.

They have been extremely communicative, upfront, and available for questions. They kept my kitten an extra night for observation d/t a change in his condition and did not charge me for the extra night. I felt he was well taken care of here.
(Also to note: they only take trupanion insurance).

Dr. Kirk and everyone on staff saved my 3 week old kitten’s life. I felt relieved as soon as I walked in the door. They took her vitals and quickly gave her oxygen. I was updated regularly and the vet had wonderful bedside manner, as well as the techs and front desk staff.
This hospital is NOT a money grab, they genuinely care about your pet and are transparent about all costs (which seem to be better than Veterinary Emergency Group btw).

It took me a while to be able to write a review, but it deserves to be shared. My experience with this hospital is only for euthanasia services for my beloved dog.

My girl 12 year old girl Luna was quoted 6-9 months due to an inoperable tumor in her chest cavity. Suddenly, only about three months into this quoted time, there was an evening where she stood up and was disoriented, breathing heavy, unfocused - and I knew it was time. In a sheer panic mode, I was looking up emergency 24/7 hospitals since it was already 9pm on a Monday when this happened (back on 7/7).

We arrived at the hospital (which I will also add looks very nice both outside and inside) and my boyfriends family ran ahead inside to get assistance. She was a big girl, so a stretcher was needed. Everyone there handled her with such immense care. They got everything set up, and let me come back and have a moment with her while they administered all of the proper medications to help her sleep easy. I literally started crying because I saw someone even cut a small heart out with the medical tape to put on her wrist where the IV was - something as small as this really truly makes such a difference both in the moment and in processing the situation after the fact.

The vet lady was seriously so kind, softly letting me know what was going on and that she wasn't in any pain. They had a little room afterwards and brought her in so we could all have a moment to say our goodbyes - they even cut some of the specific ear fur from the spot I always pet her the most, and gave it to me before I left. Since she was a big girl, her euthanasia costs were about $600 but this also included the cremation costs. She came with a beautiful wooden box, a nose print with her name (i literally cried), another big bag of her fur and even an ornament with a paw print.

If you are for any reason looking into options for your beloved pet who will be crossing the bridge soon, or plan to at home but want a back up option in case something happens - I would recommend MASH. Thank you so much for making an already seriously sad and stressful situation so much easier, and doing it with such compassion.

MASH saved our dogs life and we cannot thank them enough!!
Our Great Dane had bloat and Dr Smith came in at 3am to operate and save her. Poppy was so well cared for and looked after. We’re so thankful and grateful for the care she received here.
Thank you so much!!!

The vet was amazing and very kind. The staff... the second we walk back in to put my cat down she's throwing our carrier at us which tells my animal oh hey look I'm going home when I'm about to put her to sleep. Then all we hear is giggling and laughing the whole time we're trying to say goodbye to my cat at 2am mind you. I made them take the carrier back until we left. Very unprofessional in the worst moment of my year. I get calls about support and that I should have received paperwork about it. I didn't even get a goodbye when we talked out in tears. They were too busy laughing and giving us our empty carrier with a dirty look to worry about any paperwork. 1 paper I did get was a copy of the bill which was their biggest concern of the night, Thank you front desk. When I did just call to try to get the support packet I was put on hold for 10 minutes then hung up on.

I’m extremely upset by how my emergency call was handled. I called during a pet emergency and was first placed in an automated queue. When I called back about two hours later, the call bypassed the queue, rang repeatedly, and the same employee answered only to immediately place me on hold again for several minutes on an emergency line.

For a facility advertising emergency care, leaving a panicked client stuck in phone limbo during a breathing emergency is unacceptable.

I also asked for basic pricing information so I could understand whether I could access care. I was told the base cost was $225, and that this only covered meeting with the doctor — no testing, treatment, oxygen, bloodwork, imaging, or stabilization. I was not given even general ranges for oxygen, bloodwork, or procedures such as thoracocentesis.

I understand emergency care is expensive and estimates depend on the case, but refusing to provide even basic cost ranges while requiring payment upfront puts pet owners in an impossible position. This experience felt cold, opaque, and deeply distressing during an already terrifying emergency.

FIGURING NOW THIS IS YOUR BEST BET FOR ANY EMERGENCY NEEDS.  EVERYONE ELSE WILL CHARGE YOU A ARM A LEG AND A TOE.  FRONT DESK  JV AND MARIANO WHERE EXCELLENT DR. DEMEL WAS THE SAME. YOU CAN GOOGLE ALL YOU WANT THIS POST WILL SAVE YOU TIME. DON'T HESITATE AND WASTE TIME FOR YOUR FUR BABIES TO GET IT RIGHT,AND GO HERE! WAY OUT OF MY WAY BUT WORTH EVERY PENNY.

A few weeks ago, I was so scared I'd lose my precious dog. But coming here has given me hope. I'm so touched by the kindness and compassion of the staff. And I'm so grateful to Dr. Jeremy O'Neill, who performed Caramel's surgery. Caramel is wagging his tail in gratitude. Marshmallow also thanks you for not letting him lose his caramel.

Took my cat Roxi here when her back legs no longer worked. After talking with the team there I cam to the conclusion that it was time to let her go and put her down. The team was incredibly compassionate and supportive with this difficult decision, helped me look for other options, but was ultimately straight forward and realistic about what her likely hood of recovery was, which made the decision much easier while still being emotionally difficult. I highly highly recommend MASH to ANYONE with a pet related emergency

I had a very kind and compassionate experience with MASH. The front desk person was informative and calm even when I was a bit panicky. Bella, the vet assistant(?) was extremely sweet and helped me understand what was going on with my baby.
Dr. Duff was the person who saw my cat and did amazing work. I couldn’t be any more lucky to have such a good experience with such a great staff in such a scary moment. I highly recommend this vet, especially in an emergency situation.

READ THE ONE STAR REVIEWS!!!

I wish I had.

I spent almost fours hours in their waiting room separated from my dog. When I did finally chat with their doctor she told me the symptoms I brought my dog in for were no longer present. She wasn’t presenting any symptoms of pain or discomfort. She then told me “shes actually asleep back there”

Then proceeded to tell me that dogs of her age will sometimes act confused it’s not a big deal.

When she finally told me my dog had a fever, she followed with explanations stating it could be a symptom of a brain tumor or cancer. She continued to use technical jargon and did not explain any of it. When I inquired on the records I had provided that showed recent healthy bloodwork, CT and X Ray, she brushed it off and said all these things could have developed in the last 4 weeks.

When presented with the quote I told the tech I did not have the money for this and she replied “well how much do you have?”

They then came back with a quote for $900.

At this point I asked for fluids and took my dog home. She is much improved this morning and is eating and drinking as normal.

It felt predatory and over reaching. The attached quote is for a dog with a fever.

$6491.75- $9010.70

After reading the other reviews I can now see this is not an isolated event. I do not write reviews but this was an unbelievable price gouging situation and is unacceptable in a business that has a duty of care to their customers.
